=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5532-5744 | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` is only populated inside the retry loop, so when the cache path skips that loop the downstream `retrigger_review` path falls back to a redundant `gh api` fetch.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers agreed the settled-cache fast path leaves the iteration-local PR JSON cache empty, which defeats the intended API-hygiene reuse and adds an unnecessary GitHub API call.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5590-5598 | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The retry loop breaks only when `mergeable` is definitive and `merge_state` is non-empty and not `unknown`, so it can keep retrying even after `mergeable=false` already indicates a conflict.
  WHY: Reviewers identified that `mergeable=false` is already sufficient for a conflict decision, so waiting for `merge_state` to settle can add avoidable stall-recovery delay.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5543 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: `_STD_ITER_PR_NUM_CACHED` is initialized each iteration, but the reviewer warns the surrounding state can become inconsistent if the PR lookup fails after partial population.
  WHY: The review described this as a fragility issue around partial cache population and a possible stale/null carryover scenario.
- README.md / agents.md | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The documentation describes the early-break condition as `mergeable ∈ {true,false}` with `mergeable_state ≠ unknown`, which the reviewer said is incomplete relative to the implementation’s `dirty` shortcut.
  WHY: The review notes the implementation can break early on `mergeable_state=DIRTY` even when `mergeable` is unknown, so the docs were considered misleading in that respect.
- scripts/Orchestrate_Process.algorithms:55-98 | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The iteration-local cache is only filled inside the retry loop, so when the loop is skipped the downstream retrigger path may still make a redundant API call.
  WHY: The reviewer considered this the same cache-population gap as the shell-script finding, but reported against a different file path in its own review block.
- scripts/Orchestrate_Process.algorithms | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: There is no path that repopulates the iteration cache for settled cases when `_check_open_pr_conflict_guard` returns early.
  WHY: The reviewer framed this as a related reuse gap that compounds the redundant-call issue, but did not identify it as a correctness bug.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5590-5598 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Retry loop doesn't break when `mergeable = "false"` and `merge_state = "unknown"`, causing unnecessary delays
  WHY: Stall recovery waits up to 50s even though `mergeable = "false"` already indicates a conflict
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5532-5534, 5743-5744 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` is only populated in retry loop, leaving it empty when cache is valid and loop is skipped
  WHY: Redundant GitHub API call in `retrigger_review` action when cache hit occurs
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_STD_ITER_PR_NUM_CACHED` and `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` are only assigned inside the `if [ "${_std_conflict_should_retry}" = "true" ]` block (lines 5558-5620).
  WHY: If the cache from `_candidate_details_json` already reports a settled state (e.g. `mergeable=false`), the `should_retry` logic skips the entire retry block. Consequently, the downstream `retrigger_review` path (lines 5707-5735) finds the cache empty and performs a redundant `gh api` call to fetch the same PR JSON.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5543 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `local _STD_ITER_PR_NUM_CACHED=""`
  WHY: The variable `_STD_ITER_PR_NUM_CACHED` is initialized to empty at the start of every iteration, but the `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` companion (line 5544) is not explicitly emptied in the same way (though it is local). More importantly, if `_std_conflict_pr_num_try` is successfully determined but the fetch fails, the code may leave the state inconsistent for the downstream consumer which checks `pr_lookup_ok`.
- README.md / agents.md | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The documentation in both files describes the early break condition as: `mergeable ∈ {true,false}` AND `mergeable_state ≠ unknown`.
  WHY: The actual implementation in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (line 5598) uses an `OR` condition: `[ "${_std_attempt_merge_state}" = "dirty" ] || { ... settled ... }`. This means the loop can break even if `mergeable` is "unknown" as long as the state is "dirty". The documentation is technically incomplete/misleading regarding this shortcut.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/Orchestrate_Process.algorithms | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the cache hit shows definitive mergeability (NOT unknown), the retry loop is skipped entirely. The variable `_STD_ITER_PR_Orchestrate_CACHED` is only populated inside the retry loop, so when the loop is skipped, this cache remains empty. The downstream `retrigger_Orchestrate` path may then make a redundant `gh api` call to fetch the same PR JSON that could have been reused.
  WHY: Per the API hygiene requirements in CLAUDE.md §15, we should minimize redundant API calls. While this doesn't cause correctness issues, it does create unnecessary network overhead on each stall recovery cycle when the cache already has a definitive value.
- scripts/Orchestrate_Process.algorithms | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the cache shows a definitive non-conflicting state (e.g., mergeable=true, merge_orchestrate_state=clean), the function returns early (correctly), but there's no path that would populate the iteration-local cache with the already-fetched PR JSON for potential downstream reuse.
  WHY: This compounds Issue 1 - not only is the retry loop skipped when not needed, but even when we DO have cache data that was already fetched, we don't save it for potential reuse.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5532-5533, 5577-5578, 5743 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The iteration-local cache `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` is only populated inside the retry loop. When the GraphQL cache already shows a settled state (not `UNKNOWN`), the retry loop is skipped, leaving `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` empty. The downstream `retrigger_review` case (line 5743) then performs a redundant `gh api` call instead of reusing the prefetched data.
  WHY: The review cited the empty initialization, the in-loop assignment, and the downstream fallback path as evidence that settled-path executions still pay an unnecessary REST fetch.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5593 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The retry loop’s break condition is too strict. It requires both `mergeable` definitive (true/false) AND a non-empty, non-unknown `mergeable_state` to break early, ignoring that `mergeable=false` alone is a definitive conflict signal and `mergeable=true` alone is a definitive no-conflict signal.
  WHY: The review argued this can add unnecessary wait time when GitHub already has a definitive mergeability value but the secondary state field is still `unknown`; the review also characterized this as an optimization concern rather than a blocking correctness issue.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5546-5607, 5743-5744 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The iteration-local cache `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` is only populated inside the retry loop when `_std_conflict_should_retry` is true. When the guard skips the retry loop (cache already definitive), the cache remains empty, yet the `retrigger_review` path relies on this cache to avoid a redundant `gh api` fetch. In the skip case the guard still uses `_std_conflict_linked`, but downstream falls back to fetching the PR JSON again even though the needed `head_ref` is already available in `_std_conflict_linked`.
  WHY: The review said this wastes GitHub API calls and adds latency because the downstream fallback ignores already-available data from the settled cache path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5593-5595 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The retry loop’s break condition is too strict. It requires both `mergeable` definitive (true/false) AND a non-empty, non-unknown `mergeable_state` to break early, ignoring that `mergeable=false` alone is a definitive conflict signal and `mergeable=true` alone is a definitive no-conflict signal.
  WHY: The reviewer said this can delay conflict-resolver dispatch or normal `retrigger_review` by several retry sleeps when GitHub has already produced a definitive mergeability value but the secondary state field lags.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
